answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed challenge period before it can place orders or earn reputation. The protocol caps how much influence newly unlocked identities gain, so splitting one stake across many accounts does not multiply voting power. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital for each identity and risks losing it for provable fraud; names like lotus, plume, and sable remain labels, not credentials. This raises the cost of an attack without pretending to prevent identities from being created.
